name: graphiki
title: Graph-Based Knowledge Workspace
description: Build, explore, and analyze networks of ideas, people, and concepts with visual queries.
audience: Researchers, journalists, analysts, students, and anyone who needs to see how things connect — people whose work involves untangling relationships that are hard to hold in a spreadsheet or document.
useCases: A journalist maps the ownership structure of a group of companies — adds people, businesses, and shareholding relationships, then queries who controls what
A student organises their thesis research — links authors to papers to theories, then uses graph analysis to find the most influential sources
An analyst investigates a supply chain — builds a network of suppliers and dependencies, runs shortest-path to find single points of failure
A product manager tracks stakeholders across teams — maps who owns what, finds clusters of related work, and spots duplicated efforts using semantic similarity

dataPrivacy.storage: All data stored locally in the browser using IndexedDB. No server, no account, no data leaves your device.
dataPrivacy.export: Full graph exportable as JSON for backup or sharing.
dataPrivacy.thirdParty: ML models run locally in the browser via Web Workers. No data sent to external APIs.
dataPrivacy.offline: Fully functional offline as an installable PWA.
